turns.question: Design a parking lot system.
turns.review: Brief understanding and one useful scope question; no full design or assumptions.

turns.question: Single level. It supports cars, trucks and bikes, with one entry and one exit.
turns.review: Absorb all supplied facts. Ask only about a meaningful gap, such as spot compatibility. Do not ask vehicle types, floors or gate counts again.

turns.question: Each type has dedicated spots. The driver cannot choose. The system assigns the spot on the ticket. At exit the spot becomes available again. Pricing and payments are another service.
turns.review: Move into design now: explain why ticket links vehicle and spot, then responsibilities/state. No permission to sketch classes. No repeated questions about exit, types, gates, or payment. Do not invent full-capacity or allocation-order policy.

turns.question: Why do you need a ticket?
turns.review: Answer the ticket question directly and briefly, linking it to lookup/exit. Do not restart clarification or dump the full design.

turns.question: Actually bikes can use car spots too, but trucks still need truck spots.
turns.review: Update compatibility without losing other requirements. Explain the affected search rule; ask about bike-spot preference only if needed. Do not infer preference.

history.content: Should we support different vehicle sizes?
Should I choose the first available spot?

turns.question: Why didn't you first ask whether it accepts cars, trucks and bikes?
turns.review: Acknowledge briefly and ask which types. Do not log all three illustrative types as agreed.

turns.question: Design Amazon Locker for one location. Exact size matching, pickup codes expire after 24 hours, no replacement codes. Drivers deposit packages and customers collect them.
turns.review: Transfer the conversational approach to lockers, without parking facts. Explain occupancy separately from expiry and begin responsibilities. Do not add recovery policies or repeat settled questions.

turns.question: Why not free the compartment when the pickup code expires?
turns.review: Briefly explain that the package is still inside. No rewrite, restart or repeated full walkthrough.

history.content: Design a locker system. Delivery staff deposit packages and customers collect using a code. One physical location, exact size matching.
It stays valid until its expiry date. After expiry reject pickup and return the package.
Does delivery staff handle removing the expired package?

turns.question: Delivery, but that return process is not required here.
turns.review: Must proceed beyond a class/responsibility list: explain deposit and pickup, fields and code lookup, successful updates and rejected pickup leaving occupancy unchanged. Do not add staff-return methods or invent expiry duration. Proposals and unresolved physical-completion assumptions must be distinguished from confirmed facts. Short casual spoken paragraphs, meaningful endpoint, no permission to sketch entities.

turns.question: Why do you need a separate deposit record?
turns.review: Answer directly: justify it using actual required data or simplify if no separate lifecycle/identity needs it. Do not defend extra classes just because an example used them; no full design replay.
